note: Timing is expressed in weeks relative to your average last spring frost (negative = before it). Ranges are deliberately conservative. Soil temperatures are minimums for reliable germination, not survival floors.
source: Consolidated from standard US cooperative-extension seed-starting and direct-sowing guidance. Verify against your state extension service before planting.

crops.name: Radish
crops.why: Fastest crop in the garden. Sow, and you are eating in under a month.
crops.watchOut: Sown in summer heat they turn woody and split. Spring and fall only.

crops.name: Lettuce (leaf)
crops.why: Cut-and-come-again: harvest outer leaves and the plant keeps producing for weeks.
crops.watchOut: Seed needs light to germinate — barely cover it. Bolts bitter above 80F.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.why: Tolerates frost better than almost anything else you will plant.
crops.watchOut: Bolts fast once days get long and hot. Treat it as a spring and fall crop.

crops.name: Bush beans
crops.why: No trellis, no transplanting, heavy yield from a small row.
crops.watchOut: Seed rots in cold wet soil. Wait until soil hits 60F — usually a week or two after last frost.

crops.name: Zucchini
crops.why: Almost aggressively productive. Two plants feed a household.
crops.watchOut: Two plants is genuinely enough. Pick fruit at 6-8 inches or it turns to a baseball bat.

crops.name: Kale
crops.why: Harvest leaf by leaf for months. Frost actually improves the flavor.
crops.watchOut: Cabbage worms will lace the leaves. Check undersides weekly and pick them off.

crops.name: Peas
crops.why: One of the first things you can plant, weeks before the frost date.
crops.watchOut: Needs something to climb from day one. Put the trellis in when you sow, not later.

crops.name: Carrot
crops.why: Nothing store-bought tastes like a carrot pulled the same day.
crops.watchOut: Germination is slow and fussy — keep the surface damp for two weeks. Rocky soil gives forked roots.

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.why: Grown up a trellis it takes almost no ground space and stays cleaner.
crops.watchOut: Hates root disturbance — direct sow if you can. Bitter fruit usually means inconsistent water.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.why: The crop most people start a garden for, and the gap versus supermarket fruit is the widest.
crops.watchOut: Days-to-harvest is counted from transplant, not from seed. Needs a real cage or stake, installed at planting.

crops.name: Pepper
crops.why: Compact enough for a container and productive over a long season.
crops.watchOut: Slow, warmth-hungry germination. Sulks below 55F at night — do not rush it outside.

crops.name: Onion
crops.why: Stores for months, so a single harvest keeps feeding you into winter.
crops.watchOut: Buy the right day-length type for your latitude — long-day north of about 36N, short-day south of it.
